title: Part Twenty: Foreign Policy and the Money Flow

sections.brief: Every US government channel to Israel in Sept 2026 dollars (CPI-U 336.940): MOU fixed in nominal $ ($3.8bn ≈ $2.7bn in 2016 prices; 1985 aid ≈ $11.5bn; CRS $298bn ≈ $320bn); OSP 26.3% → $450.3m FY2025 → 0 FY2028, direct commercial contracts, Special Billing Arrangement; missile defence $14.8bn FY2006–25 and the reverse flow (co-production, US Army Iron Dome $373m 2019); loan guarantees 1992 $10bn (~$24bn) and 2003 $9bn (~$16.5bn; $4.1bn issued; to FY2030) with settlement deductions; WRSA-I, MNNA; intelligence sharing 1951–2026 (Angleton, 1981 suspension, 2009 NSA raw-data MOU, Stuxnet, post-Oct 7 drone feeds, DIA 'critical'); successor talks and the 27 Oct / 3 Nov elections. Figures: money; time

Flows in both directions: tax-deductible giving (1938 rule, American Friends; $461m 1985 → $2.06bn 2007 → $2.65bn 2021, in Sept 2026 $), settlements ($40m 2007; $224m 2009–13, Haaretz) beside loan-guarantee deductions and Israel's foreign-government NGO laws; Israel Bonds; FDI ($59.7bn US in Israel vs $22.2bn Israeli in US, 2025); goods trade 2025; arms and defence work to the US (F-35 offsets, SIPRI 7.8%, IMOD North America 13%, Twenty-Six Defense); the two-way ledger and each system's gap. Figures: stats; money
